image_description: A grey whale surfacing in calm, grey ocean waters. The whale's head and upper back are visible above the waterline, displaying a characteristic spout of mist from its blowholes. The skin appears dark grey with lighter mottling consistent with barnacle patches. No dorsal fin is visible, only the curve of the back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with a grey whale, showing an arched rostrum. A distinct spout indicates the presence of blowholes, although the holes themselves are partially obscured by the spray and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with lighter, irregular patches typical of barnacle encrustations found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only captures the anterior portion (head and shoulders) of the whale. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is submerged or outside the frame, making this feature impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and immediate shoulder area are visible. The full spindle shape and total proportions of the body cannot be assessed due to cropping/submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible upper body skin shows the correct mottled texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The whale's mouth is closed and submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external surfacing shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located ventrally and are completely submerged/occluded by the water and the angle of the photo.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is at the opposite end of the animal and is not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears textured and uneven, consistent with the rough texture and callosities associated with grey whales.

All testable checkpoints regarding head shape, skin mottling/coloration, and lack of a dorsal fin in the visible area are met. Several checkpoints were marked untestable due to the nature of the photograph (partial submersion/cropping), but there are no contradictions in the visible features. The subject is clearly identified as a grey whale based on taxonomical priors.
